To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) for a macroscopic quantum system, most wave functions are in thermal equilibrium, (ii) for a macrooscopic classical system, most phase points are in thermal equilibrium but none is in microscopic thermal equilibrium.

(1) MATE holds for all macroscopic quantum systems in a pure state; (2) MITE holds for generic macroscopic quantum systems; (3) MITE does not hold for any macroscopic classical system; and (4) MITE holds in the thermodynamic limit for all quantum many-body localized systems.

(1) For a macroscopic quantum system with a wave function, MATE holds if the wave function is in the energy shell of the microcanonical ensemble, (2) The wave function of the macroscopic quantum system is in the microcanonical ensemble if it is in the MATE, but not conversely, (3) MATE is much easier to achieve than MITE, (4) For most wave functions in a given energy shell, both MATE and the MITE are satisfied
